digest.component_or_area: S3 doctor and sync store healers
propositions: The ticket sought to extract a shared reconcile_one function used by both sync.reconverge and s3_doctor._fold_heads to eliminate duplicated merge and unrelated-history logic, but the premise was invalidated by Gerrit 1665 which removed the doctor's worktree merge entirely.

Sync and the S3 doctor hold contradictory policies on unrelated histories: sync refuses to merge when the local store carries events to prevent grafting, while the doctor unions unconditionally as pinned by held-out tests.
Sync cannot adopt the doctor's ref-only merge-tree engine because its consumers read ticket events from worktree files and would see stale pre-merge state if refs advanced without worktree updates.
The two healers employ opposed failure policies: sync must never raise and silently aborts merge failures, while the doctor must raise exceptions so the push path can abandon.

A behaviour-preserving shared reconcile_one is impossible without safety-critical policy flags, so the ticket is closed as obsolete with alternatives (thin extraction and deep unification) rejected as unsatisfactory.
